Definitions, derivations, notes, and long tables start folded.

Open questions: other choices, not tried yet

Splashery works as it is, and nothing here would replace what works. Each of these would be a separate experiment, behind the labs switch or on a comparison page, with today's behavior as the default. If you wonder "why this number?", the answer is in the notes in Levels 1 to 3, or it is "not tested yet" and listed here.

Show the table: every choice not tried yet
Choice What an experiment would show Status
A Detail slider Any splat count from 60,000 to 400,000, beside the tiers. Built as a labs slider (docs/lab/DETAIL-SLIDER.md). Built, in labs
View-dependent color A shine that moves with the view on a few kit toys, from the kit's own data and shader. Built as a private comparison, on only when a link or the address asks for it with labs on (docs/lab/GLOSS.md). Built, in labs
More moments of t Turning shapes at more than 12 moments, up to 15. Built as a labs choice (docs/lab/MOMENTS.md); more than 15 is still open. Built, in labs
240-character fields Longer fields, and what longer links cost. Built in the Splat equation toy (docs/lab/EQUATION-FIELDS.md). Built, in labs
A budget sweep on real phones Real phone graphics chips, and more phone sizes. The Kit lab's sweep (Level 2) covered five budgets, one phone size, and one software renderer. Not started
More than 15 parts A toy with 24 or 32 moving parts. The largest change: it repacks the part number, moves the part table into a texture, and needs a check on real phones. Open: no plan yet
An opacity field See-through splats in a program (and the other candidate fields in Level 3). Open: no plan yet
Formulas on the graphics chip Formulas compiled to a shader, so t is continuous and no copies are stored. Open: no plan yet

The Tinkerer's Manual, first published September 28, 2026 and updated October 11, 2026. Part of Splashery, a toy box of 3D Gaussian splats that runs in your browser. Every picture here was made with Splashery itself.
